# CLI reference

*Generated by `scripts/docgen/cli-ref`. Do not edit by hand. Run `make docs-regen` after changing `internal/cli/cli.go` or `internal/cli/catalog.go`.*

`canary` is one binary with 43 subcommands, listed here in registry order. `canary status` comes first on purpose: when anything else fails, it is the command that says whether the daemon is running and the gateway is reachable. Running `canary` with no arguments prints the grouped command summary.

Add `--json` to a data command for machine-readable output instead of a table. Commands that accept `--watch` redraw on an interval set by `--rate`, as in `canary account --watch --rate 1s`. Color is on for terminals and off for pipes; `NO_COLOR=1` turns it off, and `CANARY_COLOR=always` or `CANARY_COLOR=never` forces it either way.

The flag tables below come from the shared command catalog. Run `canary <command> --help` for the flags a command parses today, with their help text. That output is the authority if the two ever disagree.

The guard column says what a command does: `read-only` reads and prints, `local` writes local setup or configuration state, and `confirm` reaches something a human has to decide first. Where subcommands carry different guards, the summary shows the strictest one and the command's own section lists the split. The guard is documentation of behavior, not the mechanism that enforces it. The real gates live in the CLI. Standard builds have no broker-write path compiled in at all; they still preview orders, which creates no order. The separate trading build adds that path, and it still requires a verified gateway session, a submit-eligible preview token where one applies, a local journal entry, daemon authorization, and `trading.freeze` set to false. Nothing on this page grants any of that.

The group column is the heading a command appears under in `canary --help`: Desk is the account, its positions, orders and risk; Markets is broad-market regime and named-symbol technical evidence; System is running Canary itself. It is a reading aid for a long command list and says nothing about what a command may do — that is the guard.

## `canary add`

Plan a stock addition or opening and review it through existing order confirmation.

`plan` checks a stock addition or opening; `preview` creates an exact order review for separate owner confirmation through the existing order path. Neither places an order. Choose exactly one of `--quantity` or `--max`. An optional `--stop-price` applies only to added shares, uses GTC regular-session instructions, and stays held until the entry fills completely. Existing protection requires a separate review.

```sh
canary add plan SYNA --currency USD --limit 100 --quantity 3
canary add preview SYNA --currency USD --limit 100 --quantity 3 --stop-price 90 --json
```

`market` and `call-plan` read exactly one JSON object from standard input and always return JSON, even without `--json`. Unknown fields, extra objects, positional arguments and stock-only flags are rejected. These are read-only broker requests. The examples below use synthetic identities: replace the stock symbol and use the exact returned call contract, including its broker identity.

#### Stock quotes and call discovery

```sh
canary add market --json <<'JSON'
{
  "underlying": {
    "symbol": "SYNA",
    "sec_type": "STK",
    "currency": "USD",
    "exchange": "SMART"
  },
  "discover": true
}
JSON
```

| Request field | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `underlying` | Required stock contract: `symbol`, `sec_type: "STK"`, uppercase three-letter `currency`, `exchange: "SMART"`; optional known `con_id`. |
| `discover` | Optional boolean, default false. Discover call candidates for a USD stock. Omit for stock quotes alone. |
| `selected` | Optional exact call contract returned by discovery; refresh that selection. |
| `refresh` | Optional array of up to four `{"horizon_days": 30, "contract": {...}}` objects. Horizons must be unique and one of 14, 30, 60 or 120. Cannot be combined with `discover: true`. |

Calls require USD. Each selected or refreshed contract must match the underlying symbol and carry its resolved `con_id`, `sec_type: "OPT"`, `currency: "USD"`, `exchange: "SMART"`, `expiry`, positive `strike`, `right: "C"`, `multiplier: 100` and `trading_class`. Copy the returned contract rather than assembling a broker identity.

The response includes the resolved `underlying`, stock `quote`, `price_increments`, and optional `calls` or `selected` rows. Read `option_mode` (`live`, `planning`, or `unavailable`), `options_session`, and each row's `planning` or `unavailable` evidence. Closed-session planning prices are not executable quotes. Discovery grants no order authority or risk capacity.

#### Size a selected call

```sh
canary add call-plan --json <<'JSON'
{
  "contract": {
    "symbol": "SYNA",
    "con_id": 10001,
    "sec_type": "OPT",
    "currency": "USD",
    "exchange": "SMART",
    "expiry": "20300118",
    "strike": 100,
    "right": "C",
    "multiplier": 100,
    "trading_class": "SYNA"
  },
  "limit_price": 5.5,
  "budget": 5000,
  "round_size": false
}
JSON
```

| Request field | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `contract` | Required exact USD SMART call returned by `market`; same contract fields as above, with expiry `YYYYMMDD` more than seven days away. |
| `limit_price` | Required positive premium per underlying share in USD; each standard contract represents 100 shares. |
| `budget` | Required positive total USD debit including the broker fee bound, at most 1000000000. |
| `round_size` | Optional boolean, default false. Round to the nearest five contracts while retaining quantities of one or two. Rounding can exceed the budget. |

The options session must be open. Read `quantity`, `debit`, `fee_bound`, and `over_budget` before using a result; `debit` includes the fee bound. Sizing returns no submission token and reserves no money. An exact order preview and separate owner confirmation are still required.

MCP exposes stock planning through `canary_stock_add`; `market`, `call-plan` and preview are CLI surfaces, not MCP tools.

Guard `read-only`. Also available as an MCP tool.

```text
canary add plan|preview SYMBOL --currency CCY --limit PRICE (--quantity N|--max) [--con-id ID] [--stop-price PRICE] [--json]
canary add market [--json] < request.json
canary add call-plan [--json] < request.json
```

Subcommands: `plan`, `preview`, `market`, `call-plan`.

**Flags**

| Flag | Takes a value | Allowed values |
|------|---------------|----------------|
| `--limit` | yes | - |
| `--stop-price` | yes | - |
| `--quantity` | yes | - |
| `--max` | no | - |
| `--currency` | yes | - |
| `--con-id` | yes | - |
| `--exchange` | yes | - |
| `--adaptive-priority` | yes | `Normal`, `Patient`, `Urgent` |
| `--json` | no | - |

## `canary setups`

Review volume signals, find standard call options and check prices after entry; no orders or risk-limit changes.

`options` reads in three steps: listed expiries; with `--expiry`, up to 21 listed call strikes around the underlying price, which carry no prices (`status: not_requested`); with `--strike`, the exact call. Only that exact call carries a `quote`, read once within 5 seconds on a market-data line opened for this request: `status: quoted` with `bid`, `ask`, `as_of` and `data_type` when both sides are finite and positive, the bid is at most the ask, `as_of` is no more than 60 seconds old, and the broker labelled the data `live`, `delayed`, `frozen` or `delayed-frozen`. Anything else is `status: missing` with no prices. A missing quote never fails the selection, and the order preview still prices any order.

Guard `read-only`. CLI only, with no MCP tool: owner-configured entry observations ship through CLI and the typed host client first; no model tool or automatic playbook activation.

```text
canary setups evaluate --spec PATH|- --symbol SYMBOL [--con-id ID] [--at RFC3339] [--json]
canary setups options --symbol SYMBOL --con-id ID [--expiry YYYYMMDD] [--strike N] [--json]
canary setups coverage [--session YYYY-MM-DD] [--symbol SYMBOL] [--json]
canary setups markouts [--order-ref REF] [--since YYYY-MM-DD] [--symbol SYMBOL] [--json]
```

Subcommands: `evaluate`, `options`, `coverage`, `markouts`.

**Flags**

| Flag | Takes a value | Allowed values |
|------|---------------|----------------|
| `--spec` | yes | - |
| `--symbol` | yes | - |
| `--con-id` | yes | - |
| `--at` | yes | - |
| `--expiry` | yes | - |
| `--strike` | yes | - |
| `--session` | yes | - |
| `--order-ref` | yes | - |
| `--since` | yes | - |
| `--json` | no | - |

## `canary opportunities`

Review option exercise opportunities.

Opportunity detection is advisory. Only `exercise` reaches the broker; it needs an explicit human instruction for that exact action, and the standard build refuses it. `exercises` reads pending requests, revisions and available IBKR evidence. `reconcile-exercise REQUEST_REF REVISION --evidence EVIDENCE_ID --confirm-complete` records a human confirmation backed by matching broker records and sends no broker instruction. It requires an interactive human terminal; agents and MCP cannot confirm completion. Uncertain or partial requests stay blocked. See [Exercise reconciliation](../operate/orders.md#exercise-reconciliation).

Guard `confirm`. MCP exposes advisory opportunity snapshots and discovery refresh only; exercise reconciliation is CLI only.

## `canary order`

Preview, place, change, cancel or check orders.

`status` reads one journaled order and `preview` mints a tokenized draft: it runs the broker WhatIf and never transmits, and a minted token is not submit eligibility. `place`, `modify`, and `cancel` are broker writes: each requires an explicit human instruction for that exact order, and place/modify additionally consume a submit-eligible preview token through the daemon's ordinary admission gates (mode and account pins, caps, freeze, origin, journal). The constrained proposal and opportunity surfaces remain the daemon-authored candidate paths; this family is the operator's direct gated path. Every build serves `preview`; the standard build refuses `place`, `modify`, `cancel`, `tws-cancel` and `tws-modify` with `trading_disabled` before anything is sent.

Guard `read-only`, with `confirm` subcommands. Also available as an MCP tool.

```text

canary order tws-modify PERM_ID --quantity N --limit PRICE [--terms JSON] [--request-id ID] [--json]
```

## `canary stop`

Stop Canary and the mobile app server.

Stopping is local process management: it signals the daemon and the app on this machine and reaches no broker. Orders already working stay at the broker, but nothing local watches them until the daemon runs again — no fills or cancels in the journal, no protection proposals, no phone alerts. So `stop` asks before it stops a daemon that still has work in flight, the same work its own idle shutdown defers on, and `--yes` is how a script answers. `--force` only escalates a stuck process from SIGTERM to SIGKILL after `--timeout`; it never widens what is stopped. Stopping the daemon records a persistent stop intent for its socket. Ordinary CLI, MCP and app requests cannot start it again until `canary restart` clears that intent. MCP servers belong to the AI client that started them and are reported, never signalled.

Guard `confirm`. CLI only, with no MCP tool: local process-management verb (stops the daemon and app the caller is talking through); a tool call that ends order tracking and phone alerts belongs to the human at the terminal.

```text
canary stop [--app] [--daemon] [--force] [--timeout 15s] [--yes] [--json]
```

**Flags**

| Flag | Takes a value | Allowed values |
|------|---------------|----------------|
| `--app` | no | - |
| `--daemon` | no | - |
| `--force` | no | - |
| `--yes` | no | - |
| `--timeout` | yes | - |
| `--json` | no | - |
